voice.name: WTPN Grizzled - Raspy British
voice.note: grizzled older British male — a retired man in a garden-supplies hut

segments.m_open: It tore the shirt off my back, and pushed a saw down it. [pause] Two men from the Society for Psychical Research were standing in that shed watching it happen.
segments.m_s1: We were three old men selling compost. [soft laugh] That is all it was. Me, Alf Taylor and Cliff Jewiss — the Kentish Garden Guild, two sheds on the allotments at Grove Park. Seed potatoes. Fertiliser. Somewhere to go of a morning when you have finished working for a living.
segments.m_s2: It started on a spring morning. Powder went up and hit the ceiling. Then a little jug flew across the room. Cliff put that jug in a box, and shut the box — and the jug was on the floor again. [pause] After that it did not stop. Things went round the hut like skittles. A seven-pound weight went round and round Alf's head. Bags I could not lift shifted on their own.
segments.m_s3: I tried to have it out with it. I went in and did what I had been told to do, and the men outside heard the walls going and the iron doors swinging, and I came out cut and bruised. [pause] Next morning the shed looked like a bomb had hit it. And the sign of the cross was scratched and painted everywhere — the walls, the chairs, the bins. Not by any of us.
segments.m_s4: So the Society sent two of their people down — a lady and a gentleman, notebooks, the lot. And it did it in front of them. [pause] Things hanging in the air. Bolts gone off the doors. Blows on the walls hard enough to shake it. My shirt off my back and a saw shoved down it, and a bulb forced into my mouth. They wrote every bit of it down and they said what everyone said: no man could have done it.
segments.m_s5: Nearly two years, that went on, in a shed on an allotment. [exhales] I was a pensioner. I had nothing to gain, and I got hurt, and I got laughed at, and I stayed. [pause] One of them put it in a book after, and he called it my persecution — which is the right word, because it picked me. I never said I knew what it was. I know what it did to me. Make of it what you like.
